answer.effective_date: Effective December 1, 2025; Last Review October 2025; Next Review December 2026
criteria_quotes: I. Rotator cuff repair may be considered medically necessary when all of the following Criteria are met (A.-D.): A. Documentation of function-limiting pain (e.g., loss of shoulder function which interferes with the ability to carry out activities of daily living and/or demands of employment); and

B. Either of the following criteria are met: 1. Failure to respond to at least three months of non-surgical management which includes documentation of physical therapy or prescribed home exercise program and one or more of the following unless contraindicated: a. Trial of anti-inflammatory medication; or b. Cortisone injection; or 2. The individual suffers from a discrete traumatic event that results in an acute full-thickness rotator cuff tear and has associated function limiting pain; and

C. Individual meets all of the following Criteria (1. and 2.) on physical examination when compared to the non-involved side: 1. Either of the following: a. Functionally limited active range of motion; or b. Measurable loss of strength of the rotator cuff musculature; and 2. One or more of the following positive orthopedic tests/signs: a. Drop Arm Test; or b. Painful Arc Test; or c. Jobe or Empty Can Test; or d. External Rotation Lag Sign (Dropping Sign); or e. Internal Rotation Lag Sign; or f. Lift-Off Test; or g. Bear Hug Test; or h. Belly-Press Test (Napoleon); or i. Belly-Off Test; or j. Neer Impingement Test; or k. Hawkins-Kennedy Impingement; or l. Hornblower Test (Patte); and

D. Advanced diagnostic imaging study (e.g., MRI, CT) demonstrates a partial-thickness rotator cuff tear or a full-thickness rotator cuff tear that correlates with the individual's reported symptoms and physical exam findings.
answer.appeal_deadline: 180 calendar days from the date of the denial notice (2026-08-25), i.e., by 2027-02-21, per both the denial letter and Wellpoint's (Simply Healthcare's parent brand for its Florida ACA/individual line) published internal-appeal timeframe. Note: after an internal appeal decision, a further 120-calendar-day window applies to request external independent review.
answer.submission_route: Per Wellpoint's Florida Individual & Family (ACA) Complaints/Grievances/Appeals procedure — which governs Simply Healthcare Plans, Inc. d/b/a Wellpoint Florida, Inc. commercial/ACA members — an appeal of an adverse (medical necessity) determination may be filed orally or in writing: (1) Call the Member Services number on the back of the ID card, or (2) Mail a written appeal to: Wellpoint Grievances and Appeals, P.O. Box 105568, Atlanta, GA 30348-5568. Expedited appeals may be faxed to 855-298-4264 (medical/pharmacy) or 877-487-7394 (behavioral health). The appeal letter should include the member's name/ID (with 3-letter prefix), the provider's name, dates of service, the reference/claim number (POC-926BF4D7E4-25977 in this case), and any additional clinical documentation supporting medical necessity. If the internal appeal is denied, the member may request external review through an Independent Review Organization within 120 calendar days of the internal appeal resolution letter.
answer.how_to_obtain_criteria: The document above (SUR228, 'Shoulder Surgeries') was located on a public Bynder-hosted document library used by Elevance Health/Wellpoint brands, and Simply Healthcare Plans, Inc. now does business as 'Wellpoint Florida, Inc.' for its ACA marketplace product ('Wellpoint Florida Essential'), so this manual is the most likely source of the criteria applied. However, Simply/Wellpoint's own provider site (provider.simplyhealthcareplans.com/florida-provider/medical-policies-and-clinical-guidelines) requires an interactive 'guideline adoption' lookup to confirm which specific medical policies and clinical UM guidelines (including MCG-licensed guidelines) have actually been adopted for this member's specific plan/contract — the SUR228 document itself states 'This policy only applies to certain member contracts. Please check the pre-authorization website for the member contract to confirm requirements.' To be certain this is the exact criteria set applied to Emerson Delgado, the patient or provider should either (a) use that online guideline-adoption/precertification lookup tool with the member's plan ID, or (b) call the Member Services number on the ID card and explicitly request a free copy of 'the specific medical policy or clinical review criteria used to deny CPT 29827, reference POC-926BF4D7E4-25977' — Simply/Wellpoint's appeals procedure documents confirm members have a right to this on request, and the plan is obligated to include the specific clinical review criteria used in its appeal decision letter.

What was NOT independently verified is a direct, plan-specific confirmation (e.g., from Simply's own precertification/guideline-adoption lookup tool, which is interactive/JS-driven and not accessible via simple fetch) that policy SUR228 specifically, rather than a different or MCG-licensed guideline, is the one actually applied to this member's contract. After review, this request is DENIED. Reason for determination: the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity.

This determination was made under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria. You have the right to appeal this decision. Your appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of this notice (by 2027-02-21).

Reference number: POC-926BF4D7E4-25977

content.content: {"url": "https://www.wellpoint.com/content/dam/digital/wellpoint/documents/i-f/florida-complaints-grievances-and-appeals.pdf", "final_url": "https://www.wellpoint.com/content/dam/digital/wellpoint/documents/i-f/florida-complaints-grievances-and-appeals.pdf", "http_status": 200, "content_type": "application/pdf", "login_wall": false, "blocked": false, "blocked_reason": null, "error": null, "text": "IF YOU HAVE A COMPLAINT OR AN APPEAL Complaint Process A complaint is an oral or written expression of dissatisfaction with Us or with a Provider's service. Members may call the Member Services department to register a complaint. Complaints apply to any issue not related to a Medical Necessity or Experimental or Investigation determination made by Us. Complaints may be about claims processing, benefit choices, enrollment, or healthcare given to You by Your Provider. To file a complaint, please contact Us at: Wellpoint Grievances and Appeals P.O. Box 105568 Atlanta, GA 30348-5568 Phone: Call the Member Services number on Your ID Card. Appeals of Adverse Determinations and other Grievance Procedures Appeals of Adverse Determination An Adverse Determination is a coverage determination by Us that an admission, availability of care, continued stay, or other health care service has been reviewed and, based upon the information provided, does not meet the requirements for Medical Necessity, appropriateness, health care setting, level of care or effectiveness, and coverage for the requested service is therefore denied, reduced, or terminated. You or your authorized representative, may file an Appeal regarding an adverse determination for requested healthcare services and supplies. Authorized Representatives are discussed further below. An Appeal may be done orally or in writing.
